topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the learning objectives regarding cancer therapy approaches.

topics.label: Surgical, Radiotherapeutic, and Cytotoxic Approaches
topics.groupedBecause: They discuss conventional physical and cytotoxic cancer treatment modalities along with their associated mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and drug resistance.

topics.label: Targeting Tumor-Specific Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: They explore therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependence, cell cycle checkpoint loss, and defective DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Oncogenic Drivers and Kinase Inhibitor Therapies
topics.groupedBecause: They focus on targeting oncogenic driver mutations with small-molecule kinase inhibitors while examining the emergence of resistance, bypass signaling, and drug addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: They examine therapeutic strategies that utilize antibody specificity to target tumor surface markers directly or deliver conjugated cytotoxic agents.

topics.label: Cancer Immunotherapy and T-Cell Engineering
topics.groupedBecause: They explain approaches to harness and engineer the immune system to fight cancer, including immune checkpoint inhibitors, neoantigen targeting, BiTEs, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Therapeutic Challenges, Progress, and Future Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the overarching clinical challenges, historical survival outcomes, and future therapeutic directions in cancer care.
